subject: Product Specs with AI: Splitting Product and Technical Design
body:
Hello First Name,

This week's 🦄 ai that works session was on "Product Specs with AI: Splitting Product and Technical Design"!

The full recording, code, and diagrams from the session are now available on GitHub:
https://github.com/hellovai/ai-that-works

We covered a lot about how to separate product and technical questions when you're building with AI. Here's a quick summary of what we discussed:

*   **Separate Product & Technical Design**: We dove into how to clearly separate product decisions (think user experience, success metrics, and overall scope) from technical ones (like system architecture, program design, and testing). This helps everyone on the team contribute, even those less technical, while making sure the engineering is sound.
*   **Move Design Upstream**: We stressed the importance of making critical design decisions earlier in the development process. This saves a lot of headaches later, makes reviews much easier, and helps you iterate faster.
*   **AI for Better Design & Metrics**: We explored how AI can help you create useful things like HTML UI mockups for product design. It can also assist in defining clear success metrics, which helps guide your AI agents and ensures you're building towards real, measurable results.

If there's one key takeaway from the session: The best way to improve AI-assisted development is to make those critical design and verification decisions earlier in the process. It saves a lot of effort later and gives you the most impact.

Our next session next week will be all about "Agent Software Factory" – exploring how to build robust AI agent systems.

Got questions? Just reply to this email or hop into our Discord: https://www.boundaryml.com/discord. We read every message! Happy coding 🧑‍💻

Vaibhav & Dex
